subject.title: Feature: Trigger model fallback on context length exceeded

question: Should exhausted context overflow automatically replay the turn on a larger configured fallback model, and should that switch be temporary for the recovery attempt or persisted for the session?
rationale: Current main deliberately treats overflow as compaction and session recovery, while cross-model replay changes side-effect safety, context-headroom calculation, and persisted model semantics that cannot be chosen safely from implementation evidence alone.

options.title: Guarded temporary fallback
options.body: After compaction and truncation fail, retry once on a sufficiently large configured fallback without changing the persisted session model, and prohibit replay after delivery or side effects.

options.title: Persist the larger model
options.body: Switch the session to the first sufficiently large fallback after overflow recovery fails so later turns remain on that model.

options.title: Keep compaction-only recovery
options.body: Document overflow as ineligible for model fallback and improve the blocked-session recovery experience instead.

recommendation.title: Guarded temporary fallback
recommendation.body: After compaction and truncation fail, retry once on a sufficiently large configured fallback without changing the persisted session model, and prohibit replay after delivery or side effects.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent history across both decision surfaces and authored the latest substantive review of this issue.
